summary.text: Jim Walsh is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 19-Position 1, in office since January 9, 2017, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Kevin Moynihan.
He is also chair of the Washington State Republican Party and the ranking Republican on the House Civil Rights and Judiciary Committee.

paragraphs.text: Walsh was born in Jacksonville, Florida, and earned a bachelor's degree from Amherst College in 1986, according to Ballotpedia.

His House Republican biography describes him as a small business owner and writer who founded a publishing company in 1998, contributed columns to the Aberdeen Daily World and coached boys' and girls' basketball teams.
Walsh succeeded Democrat JD Rossetti in the 19th District seat.

His biography says he is the third Republican to hold the seat since the 1940s, and that he serves on three committees: ranking Republican on Civil Rights and Judiciary, member of Capital Budget and assistant ranking member of State Government and Tribal Relations.
Ballotpedia says party leadership elected him chair of the Washington Republican Party on August 12, 2023.
